high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless San Salvador Huixcolotla papel-picado illustration: one artisan cuts an agave-and-swallow pattern through a measured tissue stack beneath a rigid height stop, producing matching banners while one extra uncut sheet remains outside the frame, all formed from layered cut paper without labels or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A full cream cut-paper field carries one flat workshop composition in coral, cobalt, marigold, leaf green and black, with scalloped negative spaces confined to the outer edge and one straight dark base band beneath the figures. Every contour looks cut or punched from tissue paper. No photographic light, modeled volume, perspective room, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, diagram, skull, altar, deity, national emblem, factory machine or computer appears.

elements.desc: Rectangular Huixcolotla cutting table made from black and marigold paper shapes, with a resilient pale base and rigid cobalt bridge spanning its width. The bridge leaves one shallow fixed opening, visibly fitting the aligned working stack but not the thicker reserve bundle; it carries no ruler marks, number, written limit, lock, warning sign or arrow.

Adult papel-picado artisan standing behind the table, medium-brown skin, short wavy black hair, plain leaf-green shirt, coral trousers, dark apron and simple black shoes. With focused eyes and relaxed mouth, both hands guide a small mallet and narrow chisel through the master pattern; no badge, crown, religious garment, authority staff, written plan, electronic cutter or oversized body appears.

Precisely aligned working stack of thin coral, cobalt, marigold, leaf-green and cream tissue sheets resting on the cutting base beneath the rigid bridge. A sturdy top template carries one original secular agave-and-two-swallow design, and every sheet edge remains separately visible; the stack contains no lettering, numeral, festival slogan, skull, saint, flag, seal, interface or directional mark.

Fan of completed tissue banners suspended at upper-left, each carrying the identical pierced agave rosette, two opposing swallows and scalloped lower edge produced by the working template. Coral, cobalt, marigold, leaf-green and cream layers separate enough to show individual results while preserving exact cut geometry; no banner contains text, number, portrait, logo, religious icon, approval badge or arrow.

Single extra cobalt tissue sheet lying flat outside the cutting table at lower-right, fully intact and visibly thicker when folded with its reserve companions than the bridge opening permits. Its surface remains uncut and undamaged, showing that excess input waits outside rather than being squeezed through; it bears no rejection cross, warning label, alphabet, numeral, skull, punishment mark or tear.

Compact set of traditional hand tools resting beside the table at lower-left: one wooden mallet, three metal chisels with distinct curved tips and a small dark sharpening stone. They remain within the artisan's reach but do not touch the extra sheet; none resembles a weapon, magic wand, voting token, pointer, machine control, written key, number or authority insignia.
